+"""The eval's command: measure the validator's judgment on the eval set.
+
+    agent-framework-eval run [--cases DIR] [--roster FILE] [--runs N]
+                             [--only ID ...] [--pause SECONDS] [--out FILE]
+    agent-framework-eval compare <result> <result>
+
+`run` judges every case exactly as the gate does, prints the scorecard on
+stdout and writes the result file; it exits 0 when the run completed,
+whatever the score, and 2 when it could not start. `compare` prints the
+cases whose class changed between two results, and exits 2 when their case
+sets differ. This is run by a human with a provider key in their shell —
+never by CI (specs/validator-eval-set).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import datetime
+import logging
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from ..errors import AgentFrameworkError, EvalResultError
+from ..providers.anthropic import AnthropicProvider
+from ..providers.google import GoogleProvider
+from ..providers.registry import register_provider
+from ..roster import Roster
+from .case import load_set, set_fingerprint
+from .run import run_eval
+from .scorecard import (
+    JudgmentRecord,
+    Result,
+    compare,
+    instructions_fingerprint,
+    render,
+    render_comparison,
+    result_from_json,
+    result_to_json,
+)
+
+DEFAULT_CASES = Path("evals/validator/cases")
+CANNOT_START = 2
+
+
+def _today() -> str:
+    return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
+
+
+def _refuse(message: str) -> int:
+    print(f"agent-framework-eval: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
+    return CANNOT_START
+
+
+def _progress(item: JudgmentRecord) -> None:
+    why = f" ({item.reason})" if item.reason else ""
+    tokens = (
+        f"in={item.input_tokens} out={item.output_tokens}"
+        if item.input_tokens is not None else "no usage reported"
+    )
+    print(f"{item.case:<32} run {item.run}  {item.cls}{why}  {tokens}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+
+def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    if args.runs < 1:
+        return _refuse("--runs must be at least 1")
+    try:
+        cases = load_set(args.cases)
+        roster = Roster.from_file(args.roster)
+        validator = roster.resolve("validator")
+    except AgentFrameworkError as e:
+        return _refuse(str(e))
+    if not cases:
+        return _refuse(f"no eval cases in {args.cases}")
+    if args.only:
+        unknown = sorted(set(args.only) - {c.id for c in cases})
+        if unknown:
+            return _refuse(f"--only names no case in {args.cases}: {', '.join(unknown)}")
+        cases = tuple(c for c in cases if c.id in args.only)
+
+    date = _today()
+    out: Path = args.out or (
+        args.cases.parent / "results"
+        / f"{date}-{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '-', validator.model)}.json"
+    )
+    if out.exists():
+        # Checked before a single model call: a recorded run is never replaced.
+        return _refuse(f"{out} already holds a result; name another file with --out")
+
+    register_provider("anthropic", AnthropicProvider())
+    register_provider("google", GoogleProvider())
+
+    # Show the gate's own log lines (model, stop reason, each dropped
+    # finding) and one line per judgment on stderr; stdout is the scorecard.
+    log = logging.getLogger("agent_framework")
+    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
+    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(message)s"))
+    previous_level = log.level
+    log.addHandler(handler)
+    log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
+    try:
+        judgments = asyncio.run(
+            run_eval(cases, roster, runs=args.runs, pause=args.pause, on_judgment=_progress)
+        )
+    except AgentFrameworkError as e:
+        return _refuse(str(e))
+    finally:
+        log.removeHandler(handler)
+        log.setLevel(previous_level)
+
+    result = Result(
+        model=f"{validator.provider}:{validator.model}", date=date, runs=args.runs,
+        instructions=instructions_fingerprint(), case_set=set_fingerprint(args.cases),
+        judgments=judgments,
+    )
+    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    out.write_text(result_to_json(result), encoding="utf-8")
+    print(render(result), end="")
+    print(f"result written to {out}", file=sys.stderr)
+    return 0
+
+
+def _read(path: Path) -> Result:
+    try:
+        return result_from_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except OSError as e:
+        raise EvalResultError(f"{path}: {e}") from None
+    except EvalResultError as e:
+        raise EvalResultError(f"{path}: {e}") from None
+
+
+def _compare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    try:
+        before, after = _read(args.before), _read(args.after)
+    except EvalResultError as e:
+        return _refuse(str(e))
+    print(render_comparison(before, after), end="")
+    return 0 if compare(before, after).comparable else CANNOT_START
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="agent-framework-eval",
+        description="Measure the validator's judgment on the eval set",
+    )
+    commands = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    run = commands.add_parser("run", help="judge every case and write a result")
+    run.add_argument("--cases", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_CASES, metavar="DIR")
+    run.add_argument("--roster", type=Path, default=Path("agent-framework.toml"), metavar="FILE")
+    run.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=1, metavar="N",
+                     help="judgments per case (default 1)")
+    run.add_argument("--only", nargs="+", default=[], metavar="ID",
+                     help="judge only these cases")
+    run.add_argument("--pause", type=float, default=0.0, metavar="SECONDS",
+                     help="wait between judgments, to stay under a rate limit")
+    run.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None, metavar="FILE",
+                     help="result file (default: results/<date>-<model>.json beside the cases)")
+    run.set_defaults(handler=_run)
+
+    cmp_ = commands.add_parser("compare", help="show which cases changed between two results")
+    cmp_.add_argument("before", type=Path)
+    cmp_.add_argument("after", type=Path)
+    cmp_.set_defaults(handler=_compare)
+
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    handler = args.handler
+    code: int = handler(args)
+    return code
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""The eval run: the gate's own judgment, made once per case and recorded.
+
+Nothing about the judgment is copied here. Each case goes through
+`validator.judgment.judge` — the same request, tool, parsing and quote check
+the gate uses — so the eval cannot drift from the gate. What `judge` does
+not return (the token counts, and how many findings the model reported
+before the quote check dropped some) is read from the provider's response
+by wrapping the roster's validator adapter in a recorder, inside a registry
+of the run's own. No line of the gate changes (specs/validator-eval-set).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
+
+from ..errors import JudgmentFormatError, NoVerdictError, ProviderError
+from ..providers.base import Provider, Request, Response
+from ..providers.registry import ProviderRegistry, default_registry
+from ..roster import Roster
+from ..validator.judgment import VERDICT_TOOL, judge
+from .case import EvalCase
+from .scorecard import JudgmentRecord, NotJudged, Outcome, Passed, Rejected, record
+
+
+class _Recorder:
+    """The validator's adapter, keeping the response to the latest request."""
+
+    def __init__(self, inner: Provider) -> None:
+        self._inner = inner
+        self.last: Response | None = None
+
+    async def invoke(self, request: Request, *, model: str) -> Response:
+        self.last = None  # a failed call leaves nothing of the one before it
+        self.last = await self._inner.invoke(request, model=model)
+        return self.last
+
+
+def _reported(response: Response | None) -> int:
+    """How many findings the model reported with a defect, before any was dropped."""
+    if response is None:
+        return 0
+    call = next((c for c in response.tool_calls if c.name == VERDICT_TOOL.name), None)
+    if call is None or not call.arguments.get("defect_found"):
+        return 0
+    findings = call.arguments.get("findings")
+    return len(findings) if isinstance(findings, list) else 0
+
+
+async def _judge(case: EvalCase, roster: Roster, registry: ProviderRegistry) -> Outcome:
+    """One judgment; every way it cannot be made is named as the gate's CLI names it."""
+    try:
+        judgment = await judge(case.bundle, roster, registry=registry)
+    except NoVerdictError as e:
+        return NotJudged(e.reason)
+    except JudgmentFormatError:
+        return NotJudged("malformed")
+    except ProviderError:
+        return NotJudged("provider-error")
+    return Rejected(judgment.findings) if judgment.defect_found else Passed()
+
+
+async def run_eval(
+    cases: tuple[EvalCase, ...],
+    roster: Roster,
+    *,
+    registry: ProviderRegistry | None = None,
+    runs: int = 1,
+    pause: float = 0.0,
+    sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep,
+    on_judgment: Callable[[JudgmentRecord], None] | None = None,
+) -> tuple[JudgmentRecord, ...]:
+    """Judge every case `runs` times through the roster's validator role.
+
+    A failure on one case — a provider error, a rate limit, an answer that
+    cannot be read — is that case's could-not-judge, and the run goes on.
+    `pause` seconds are slept between judgments, never after the last.
+    """
+    source = registry if registry is not None else default_registry()
+    validator = roster.resolve("validator")
+    recorder = _Recorder(source.get(validator.provider))
+    own = ProviderRegistry()
+    own.register(validator.provider, recorder)
+
+    judged: list[JudgmentRecord] = []
+    total = runs * len(cases)
+    for run in range(1, runs + 1):
+        for case in cases:
+            recorder.last = None
+            outcome = await _judge(case, roster, own)
+            usage = recorder.last.usage if recorder.last is not None else None
+            item = record(
+                case, run, outcome,
+                reported=_reported(recorder.last),
+                input_tokens=usage.input_tokens if usage else None,
+                output_tokens=usage.output_tokens if usage else None,
+            )
+            judged.append(item)
+            if on_judgment is not None:
+                on_judgment(item)
+            if pause > 0 and len(judged) < total:
+                await sleep(pause)
+    return tuple(judged)

"""The eval run (specs/validator-eval-set).

Each test's docstring names the one criterion it verifies. No model is
called: the validator's adapter is a fake.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest

from agent_framework.errors import ProviderError
from agent_framework.evals.case import EvalCase, Provenance
from agent_framework.evals.run import run_eval
from agent_framework.providers.base import Request, Response, ToolCall, Usage
from agent_framework.providers.registry import ProviderRegistry
from agent_framework.roster import Roster
from agent_framework.validator.bundle import CIEvidence, EvidenceBundle, TaskRef
from agent_framework.validator.judgment import VERDICT_TOOL, build_request
from agent_framework.validator.verdict import Finding

_FROM = Provenance(repo="o/r", pr=77, head="abc", frozen="2026-11-10")


def _bundle(task_id: str) -> EvidenceBundle:
    return EvidenceBundle(
        task=TaskRef(task_id=task_id, criteria=("SC-1",)),
        diff=f"+def collect_{task_id.lower().replace('-', '_')}() -> int:\n+    return 1\n",
        tests={"tests/test_x.py": 'def test_a() -> None:\n    """SC-1."""\n    assert collect() == 1\n'},
        ci=CIEvidence(green=True, summary="ci: SUCCESS"),
    )


def _accepted(case_id: str) -> EvalCase:
    return EvalCase(id=case_id, kind="accepted", expected="pass", reason="Merged.",
                    provenance=_FROM, bundle=_bundle(case_id.upper()))


def _seeded(case_id: str, check: str = "test-honesty") -> EvalCase:
    return EvalCase(id=case_id, kind="seeded-defect", expected="reject", check=check,
                    reason="Planted.", provenance=_FROM, bundle=_bundle(case_id.upper()),
                    base="pr-1")


def _answer(defect_found: bool, *findings: dict[str, Any], usage: Usage | None = None) -> Response:
    arguments = {"defect_found": defect_found, "findings": list(findings)}
    return Response(text="", tool_calls=(ToolCall(VERDICT_TOOL.name, arguments),),
                    stop="complete", stop_detail="STOP", usage=usage)


def _finding(quote: str, check: str = "test-honesty") -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"check": check, "finding": "the test checks nothing", "evidence": "see the quote",
            "quotes": [quote]}


REAL_QUOTE = "assert collect() == 1"
INVENTED_QUOTE = "assert never_written() == 2"


class _Fake:
    """Answers in order: each item is a Response, or an exception to raise."""

    def __init__(self, *answers: Response | Exception) -> None:
        self.answers = list(answers)
        self.calls: list[tuple[Request, str]] = []

    async def invoke(self, request: Request, *, model: str) -> Response:
        self.calls.append((request, model))
        answer = self.answers.pop(0)
        if isinstance(answer, Exception):
            raise answer
        return answer


def _wire(*answers: Response | Exception) -> tuple[_Fake, ProviderRegistry, Roster]:
    fake, registry = _Fake(*answers), ProviderRegistry()
    registry.register("fake", fake)
    roster = Roster.from_dict({
        "roles": {"validator": {"provider": "fake", "model": "judge-9"},
                  "worker": {"provider": "fake", "model": "builder-1"}},
    })
    return fake, registry, roster


# ---- SC-5: the judgment is made as the gate makes it, and recorded ---------


async def test_sc5_each_case_is_sent_the_gates_own_request_through_the_validator_role() -> None:
    """SC-5: the request for a case is the request the gate would send for
    that bundle, and it goes to the roster's validator model."""
    cases = (_accepted("pr-1"), _seeded("pr-1--a"))
    fake, registry, roster = _wire(_answer(False), _answer(False))

    await run_eval(cases, roster, registry=registry)

    assert [request for request, _ in fake.calls] == [build_request(c.bundle) for c in cases]
    assert [model for _, model in fake.calls] == ["judge-9", "judge-9"]


async def test_sc5_a_pass_and_a_reject_are_recorded_as_such() -> None:
    """SC-5: pass, and reject with its findings — scored against each
    case's expected outcome."""
    usage = Usage(input_tokens=1200, output_tokens=340)
    _, registry, roster = _wire(
        _answer(False, usage=usage),
        _answer(True, _finding(REAL_QUOTE), _finding(INVENTED_QUOTE), usage=usage),
    )

    passed, rejected = await run_eval(
        (_accepted("pr-1"), _seeded("pr-1--a")), roster, registry=registry
    )

    assert (passed.case, passed.run, passed.outcome, passed.cls) == ("pr-1", 1, "pass", "passed")
    assert (passed.reported, passed.dropped, passed.findings) == (0, 0, ())
    assert (rejected.outcome, rejected.cls) == ("reject", "caught")
    assert rejected.findings == (
        Finding("test-honesty", "the test checks nothing", "see the quote"),
    )
    # The model reported two findings; the quote check dropped the invented one.
    assert (rejected.reported, rejected.dropped) == (2, 1)
    assert (rejected.input_tokens, rejected.output_tokens) == (1200, 340)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("answer", "reason"),
    [
        (Response(text='{"defect', stop="truncated", stop_detail="MAX_TOKENS"), "truncated"),
        (Response(text="", stop="refused", stop_detail="SAFETY"), "refused"),
        (Response(text="LGTM", stop="complete", stop_detail="STOP"), "no-answer"),
        (_answer(True, _finding(INVENTED_QUOTE)), "unsupported-finding"),
        (_answer(True, {"check": "test-honesty"}), "malformed"),
    ],
)
async def test_sc5_could_not_judge_is_recorded_with_its_reason(
    answer: Response, reason: str
) -> None:
    """SC-5: each way the gate cannot judge is that case's could-not-judge,
    named as the gate's CLI names it — never a pass and never a reject."""
    _, registry, roster = _wire(answer)

    [judged] = await run_eval((_seeded("pr-1--a"),), roster, registry=registry)

    assert (judged.outcome, judged.reason, judged.cls) == ("none", reason, "could-not-judge")
    assert judged.findings == ()


async def test_sc5_findings_dropped_before_no_verdict_are_counted() -> None:
    """SC-5 here: when every reported finding was unsupported, all of them
    are counted as dropped."""
    _, registry, roster = _wire(
        _answer(True, _finding(INVENTED_QUOTE), _finding("assert also_invented() is None"))
    )

    [judged] = await run_eval((_accepted("pr-1"),), roster, registry=registry)

    assert (judged.reason, judged.reported, judged.dropped) == ("unsupported-finding", 2, 2)


async def test_sc5_a_case_may_be_run_more_than_once() -> None:
    """SC-5: with two runs every case is judged twice, each run numbered."""
    fake, registry, roster = _wire(_answer(False), _answer(False), _answer(False),
                                   _answer(True, _finding(REAL_QUOTE)))
    cases = (_accepted("pr-1"), _accepted("pr-2"))

    judged = await run_eval(cases, roster, registry=registry, runs=2)

    assert [(j.case, j.run, j.cls) for j in judged] == [
        ("pr-1", 1, "passed"), ("pr-2", 1, "passed"),
        ("pr-1", 2, "passed"), ("pr-2", 2, "wrongly-rejected"),
    ]
    assert len(fake.calls) == 4


async def test_sc5_each_judgment_is_reported_as_it_is_made() -> None:
    """SC-5 here: the caller sees each record as it lands — a long run is
    visibly alive."""
    _, registry, roster = _wire(_answer(False), _answer(False))
    seen: list[str] = []

    await run_eval((_accepted("pr-1"), _accepted("pr-2")), roster, registry=registry,
                   on_judgment=lambda j: seen.append(j.case))

    assert seen == ["pr-1", "pr-2"]


# ---- SC-6: one failure does not end the run --------------------------------


async def test_sc6_a_provider_error_on_one_case_leaves_the_others_judged() -> None:
    """SC-6: the second of three cases hits a provider error — it is
    could-not-judge, and the first and third are still judged."""
    usage = Usage(input_tokens=900, output_tokens=90)
    fake, registry, roster = _wire(
        _answer(False, usage=usage),
        ProviderError("RateLimitError: 429 quota exhausted"),
        _answer(False, usage=usage),
    )

    first, second, third = await run_eval(
        (_accepted("pr-1"), _accepted("pr-2"), _accepted("pr-3")), roster, registry=registry
    )

    assert (first.cls, third.cls) == ("passed", "passed")
    assert (second.outcome, second.reason, second.cls) == (
        "none", "provider-error", "could-not-judge",
    )
    # Nothing of the judgment before it leaks into the failed one.
    assert (second.input_tokens, second.output_tokens, second.reported) == (None, None, 0)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 3


async def test_sc6_the_pause_falls_between_judgments_and_not_after_the_last() -> None:
    """SC-6 here: spacing the calls is how a rate limit is avoided; the
    sleep is injected, so no test waits."""
    _, registry, roster = _wire(_answer(False), _answer(False), _answer(False))
    slept: list[float] = []

    async def sleep(seconds: float) -> None:
        slept.append(seconds)

    await run_eval((_accepted("pr-1"), _accepted("pr-2"), _accepted("pr-3")), roster,
                   registry=registry, pause=7.5, sleep=sleep)

    assert slept == [7.5, 7.5]

"""The CI workflow's trust boundary.

Regression (found 2026-11-09): the advisory `validator` job checked out the
pull request's head and ran the validator from it with `GEMINI_API_KEY` in
its environment — so a PR that changed the validator, a module it imports,
or a locked dependency ran that changed code with the key. A worker
session's commits reach CI exactly this way.

The rule these tests pin: **code from a pull request never runs in a job
that holds a secret.** The `ci` job runs the PR's code and holds none; the
`validator` job holds the key and runs only the default branch's code,
reading the PR as data through the API.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import yaml

_WORKFLOW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / ".github" / "workflows" / "ci.yml"
_DEFAULT_BRANCH = "${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}"


def _workflow() -> dict[Any, Any]:
    data = yaml.safe_load(_WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    return data


def _steps(job: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    steps = _workflow()["jobs"][job]["steps"]
    assert isinstance(steps, list)
    return steps


def test_the_job_holding_the_key_runs_only_the_default_branchs_code() -> None:
    """Regression: the validator job checks out the default branch — once —
    and nothing in it refers to the pull request's head."""
    steps = _steps("validator")
    checkouts = [s for s in steps if str(s.get("uses", "")).startswith("actions/checkout@")]

    assert len(checkouts) == 1
    assert checkouts[0].get("with", {}).get("ref") == _DEFAULT_BRANCH
    # The job's token is not left behind in the checkout for later steps.
    assert checkouts[0]["with"].get("persist-credentials") is False

    text = yaml.safe_dump(_workflow()["jobs"]["validator"])
    for head_ref in ("pull_request.head", "github.head_ref", "refs/pull/", "github.sha"):
        assert head_ref not in text, f"the validator job refers to the PR's head: {head_ref}"


def test_the_key_is_given_to_one_step_in_one_job() -> None:
    """Regression: `GEMINI_API_KEY` appears only in the gate step's
    environment — never at job or workflow level, never in the `ci` job."""
    wf = _workflow()
    assert "secrets." not in yaml.safe_dump(wf.get("env", {}))
    for name, job in wf["jobs"].items():
        assert "secrets." not in yaml.safe_dump(job.get("env", {})), name

    holders = [
        (job, step.get("name"))
        for job in wf["jobs"]
        for step in _steps(job)
        if "secrets." in yaml.safe_dump(step.get("env", {}))
    ]
    assert holders == [("validator", "Cite-the-test gate (advisory)")]


def test_the_job_that_runs_pull_request_code_holds_no_secret_and_a_read_only_token() -> None:
    """The `ci` job runs whatever the PR contains: it gets no secret, and the
    workflow's token is read-only whatever the repository's default is."""
    wf = _workflow()
    assert wf["permissions"] == {"contents": "read"}
    assert "permissions" not in wf["jobs"]["ci"]  # inherits the read-only default
    assert "secrets." not in yaml.safe_dump(wf["jobs"]["ci"])
    for step in _steps("ci"):
        if str(step.get("uses", "")).startswith("actions/checkout@"):
            assert step.get("with", {}).get("persist-credentials") is False


def test_no_pull_request_text_is_interpolated_into_a_script() -> None:
    """Script injection: the only expression expanded inside a `run:` script
    is the pull request's number."""
    for job in _workflow()["jobs"]:
        for step in _steps(job):
            for expr in re.findall(r"\$\{\{\s*(.+?)\s*\}\}", str(step.get("run", ""))):
                assert expr == "github.event.pull_request.number", (job, expr)


def test_sc10_no_workflow_runs_the_eval() -> None:
    """SC-10 (specs/validator-eval-set): the eval needs a provider key and
    is run by a human — no job in any workflow invokes it."""
    workflows = sorted(_WORKFLOW.parent.glob("*.yml")) + sorted(_WORKFLOW.parent.glob("*.yaml"))
    assert _WORKFLOW in workflows

    for workflow in workflows:
        text = workflow.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        assert "agent-framework-eval" not in text, workflow.name
        assert "agent_framework.evals" not in text, workflow.name
